Detection-event sampling via stim m2d: a FIXED measurement record is converted to detection events and observable flips against a circuit. Unlike stim detect, m2d does no sampling - it is a pure function of (circuit, measurement data), so this check is DETERMINISTIC where the frame-simulator check is not. It exercises measurements_to_detection_events, which this module owns. Policy is invariants only because the measurement record itself is generated by a seeded sample; the m2d reduction of it is exact.

VARIANT: seed 8675309 -> 8675310, an independent sampling stream. The measurement record that m2d consumes is produced by a seeded sample, and stim's own --seed documentation states results MAY NOT be consistent across machine architectures, so the record a port produces will differ. What must be proven achievable is that the STATISTICS of the m2d reduction are stable across independent records, which is what a fresh seed measures. The seed-to-seed spread is the Monte Carlo error the tolerance must admit.
